prompt:
Paint ONE building for a top-down pixel-art JRPG town map, in the classic 3/4 top-down RPG view: the roof is seen from above (it fills the upper coloured block of the guide) and the front wall is seen straight on (the lower block). The attached image is an exact layout guide drawn at the final proportions: keep the outer silhouette, the roof/wall split line, the door (dark brown rectangle: it must stay exactly there, same size, at ground level, a real door you can walk through) and the windows (yellow rectangles) in exactly the same places. You may add small details (eaves, trim, drainpipe, flower boxes, crates by the wall, a chimney poking above the roof into the empty top margin).
This building: a small house in a misty lake town built on stilts over shallow water. Dark wooden shingle roof. Weathered grey-green planks on stilts, a narrow wooden walkway in front, round lamps. Windows glow warm amber from inside (the only light). The whole image is 176 x 160 art pixels (each art pixel 7x7 image pixels).
Premium modern hi-bit 2D pixel art ("HD pixel art" JRPG look), hand-placed pixels. Every art pixel is a crisp square of the same size across the whole image (about 8x8 image pixels per art pixel). No anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft brushes, no photographic texture, no noise, no dithering checkerboards. Clusters of 3-10 pixels with clear shapes. Hue-shifted colour ramps: shadows lean toward purple/red and are more saturated, highlights lean toward warm yellow. 4-6 shades per material, rich but earthy, worn and lived-in.
Lighting: neutral, soft, even light from the upper left, like a calm overcast evening; NO cast shadows, NO night darkness, NO lamp light pools, NO vignette. (The game engine adds the night lighting on top later, so this must be the clean base colours.)
Background: fully transparent (the magenta in the guide is background). No ground, no shadow, no people, no text, no letters.
revised_prompt: Edit the supplied exact layout guide into ONE small stilt house for a misty lake-town JRPG map. Treat the attached image as a STRICT pixel-coordinate mask/layout, not merely inspiration. Final canvas 1232x1120 (176x160 art pixels, enlarged by exactly 7 with nearest-neighbor): all art pixels are sharp uniform 7x7 squares. Preserve original outer house silhouette and boundaries: roof x=14..1218, y=196..714, with horizontal roof/front division at y=423..437; wall x=56..1176, y=715..1119; dark brown actual ground-level door x=539..693 y=896..1119; left amber window x=238..350 y=896..1037, right amber window x=868..980 y=896..1037. Keep windows and door same size, exactly same place, including their framing, do not shift or obstruct them. Roof is seen from ABOVE as one broad rectangular plane, with dark wooden shingle rows, staggered individually readable blocky shingles, subtle worn purple-charcoal shadows and muted warm weathered highlights. Lower wall straight-on, weathered grey-green horizontal plank siding with orderly dark seams; small faded bracing, trim and eaves. Wooden stilts just visible immediately beneath building and a VERY narrow plank walkway along the front bottom edge without moving door bottom or changing base footprint. Two tiny unlit round lamps in subdued materials near front, NO emitted glow from lamps; only the windows emit steady amber color, without exterior light spill. Preserve empty margin above roof, optional small chimney there. Everything outside the building silhouette including original magenta guide must become truly transparent alpha, not colored background. No ground or water or shadows. Premium carefully hand-placed hi-bit pixel-art JRPG asset, stylish hue shifted limited 4-6 tone ramps for each material, sharp medium-size deliberate pixel clusters, rich earthy color. Neutral even soft overcast evening ambient light upper left, no night-darkening, no cast shadows, no light pools, no gradients, no blur, no antialiasing, no noise, no dithering, no text, no people. Retain precisely the guide's direct orthographic 3/4 RPG roof-top/front-wall view, not an isometric building with visible side walls.
